candidates.title: PRT epoch listener keeps every input of every open epoch in process memory about three times over (hex log in the history plus raw bytes), in addition to the stored player's on-disk copy
candidates.component: PRT player process: doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua (poll, self.inputs, self.history), doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua (logs retained per address), doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua (inputs shared by reference), started by crisium.lua
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI'). It stands in for the honest operator's chain observation.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua poll() lines 30-82 (history:get_logs keeps every InputAdded log, with its ABI-encoded input as a hex string, for the whole epoch and the whole dispute; line 80 self.inputs[#self.inputs + 1] = data keeps the raw bytes); prt-epoch.lua 106-130 passes inputs = self.inputs to the bridge; prt-log-history.lua fetch() lines 84-93 appends each log table to self.logs[address] and never drops it before the listener is dropped (crisium.lua pass() lines 318-331, only once the epoch is finished); doc/recipes/prt.lua stored_player_methods:store_input (2585-2590) already keeps every input on disk in the epoch directory.
candidates.description: For each open epoch (accumulating, or sealed until its settlement is irreversible and its jobs are gone) the listener's log history retains every InputAdded log table decoded from JSON, whose data field is the hex text of the ABI-encoded input (about 2x the input size), and the listener retains the raw input bytes in self.inputs (1x), which the bridge uses only to encode the delivery prefix of a leaf proof at a single input slot. The stored honest player already keeps a durable copy of each input in its epoch directory, which read_input serves. Measured with the real prt-log-history fetch path and prt-ethereum decoding on a fake chain: the retained heap per 65,508-byte input is about 64 KiB of raw bytes on top of the ~128 KiB hex log, i.e. ~192 KiB of RAM per input, so an epoch filled to the per-epoch input limit (2^24 inputs of the InputBox's maximum size) needs on the order of 3 TiB of RAM in one Lua process, and crisium keeps it for every open epoch at once. On a restart, all of it is fetched and rebuilt again.
candidates.trigger: Any input sender (THREAT_MODEL section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts, with payloads chosen to maximize the honest operator's cost (R12)'). The sender adds many maximum-size inputs to the application's InputBox during an epoch; the player must process the on-chain input record.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: inputs are chosen by any party and the InputBox caps only the per-input size; DaveConsensus caps an epoch at 2^24 inputs. The amount an adversary can actually push into one epoch is bounded by the chain's calldata throughput and fees during the epoch, not by the player.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion fits: the trigger is inputs, which the honest operator 'must process the on-chain input record' (section 4); it is not an application stall, output flood (inputs, not outputs), host fault or reorg. 2. Role: support (player/listener). 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... Any other support defect is Low.' 3. High/Medium cases: R12 says 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain, keeping and persisting its own records, and restarting, has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match, and its total grows only with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open.' The retained memory is bounded per input (~3x its bytes) and grows only with open epochs' inputs, so the R12 wording is met; the High constant-factor case speaks of 'an operation listed in R12', and chain observation is not in that list. If triage reads the deployment's sizing as disk-sized for inputs (the stored player's copy) and not RAM-sized at 3x, the honest-operator rating would be High ('a crash ... or unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role' is not it; the constant-factor High entry would be), giving Medium in support. 4. Critical: no rule is violated at the per-input level. 5. Low: otherwise Low. Claimed: Low (Medium only under the sizing reading above).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not break the goal by itself. It makes process RAM, rather than disk, the resource that bounds how many inputs per epoch the reference player can defend; an out-of-memory crash would repeat after every relaunch (the relaunch refetches and rebuilds the same data) and stop every match of every epoch in that process.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r2/DFCHAIN/mem.lua (lua5.4 with bugs/env.sh): 64 synthetic InputAdded logs of 65,508-byte inputs served as JSON through a fake chain into prt-log-history.get_logs and prt-ethereum abi:event; the heap retained after freeing the JSON text grew by 65.0 KiB per input over the ~128 KiB hex log already held by the history.
candidates.test_idea: With a fake chain, run prt-epoch.new(...):poll() over N maximum-size InputAdded logs and a stored player; assert that the Lua heap retained by the listener and its history after the poll is O(1) per input beyond a small constant (e.g. below 4 KiB per input), i.e. that input bytes are served from the player's durable copy or refetched on demand when a leaf proof needs them.

not_covered: Checked and refuted (no candidate): crisium.lua get_seal() observes the consensus at the latest block, not under --input-policy, and its result fixes the next listener's input_begin and first_input_block; but open_epochs() opens epoch N only once checkpoints/epoch-N exists, which the epoch N-1 player writes only on the EpochSealed(N-1) that the N-1 listener observed under the input policy, so the seal is already final (or as deep as a numeric policy) when get_seal reads it.

Checked (no candidate): every address the bridge and listener fetch is trusted Dave/Rollups code (factory, consensus, root from EpochSealed, children from NewInnerTournament, InputBox filtered by InputAdded+app topic); adversary-instantiated factory tournaments are dropped by the address==root check; no adversary-deployed contract's logs reach the decoder. Event ABI entries keyed by topic0 have no signature collisions with different indexed layouts among the five artifacts; no event parameter is named name/address/log.

Checked (no candidate): cartesi.evmu decoding of the fetched events (static types plus one bytes field) is bounds-checked; eth.small conversions are applied only to fields bounded below 2^63 by the contracts (positions < 2^62, instants, counts).

Checked (no candidate): bridge job derivation (responder parity, leaf race windows, winMatchByTimeout/eliminate windows, inner-tournament winner/expiry windows, can_join closure vs Time.timeoutElapsed) against Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 Tournament/Match semantics; reveal_bisection/seal_divergence use only the player's own tree and the event's waiting-side left node; the child claim's contested-state assert holds for the honest lineage.

Checked (no candidate): adversary front-running (copying the honest commitment, advancing or sealing the honest match on its behalf) is handled by the joined-by-anyone binding and event-keyed jobs; Dave rejects duplicate commitments.

Checked (no candidate): the native/Solidity disagreement assert in prt-bridge attempt() (R1-A8-2) has no adversary trigger I could find: the simulate runs at the observation head inside the leaf race window, the provider's epoch bounds cannot move while a leaf match of this epoch is live (the root cannot finish before its children), and the proof's input bytes are the InputBox bytes.

Checked (no candidate): RPC error-code asserts (code 3 for preflight, estimate and proof simulation). Dave, the regenerated step and rollups-contracts have no bare require/revert(0,0); honest actions revert only with custom errors (code 3). I did not verify behaviour of every node implementation for reverts with empty data (geth older versions return -32000), nor calldata-slice out-of-bounds reverts, which only malformed proofs reach.

Checked (no candidate): prt-log-history paging, rewind and common-ancestor logic (no duplicate or lost logs found by reading); removal of stale inputs/*.bin past input_count on stored-player reopen (fs.clone_file uses O_EXCL, but reopen_epoch_directory removes them).
Not covered: prt-rpc.lua and prt-websocket.lua framing and JSON robustness against a misbehaving node (the node is trusted, section 4); dkjson depth/size limits.

Not covered: gas-limit sufficiency of 2x eth_estimateGas when an adversary changes state between estimation and inclusion (e.g. creating a dangling commitment so a win also pairs); not measured on the chain harness.
Not covered: fee-market effects on prt-transactions (base-fee spikes against --max-fee, eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas manipulation), considered chain-inclusion assumptions.

Not covered: the stageTournamentResult terminal path (self.terminal makes crisium exit by assert and crash-loop) for epochs whose final state is not an accepted yield; I judged it an application stall with only bond recovery lost and did not report it.

Not covered: Arbitrum deployments, where block.number is the parent chain's block while the bridge compares eth_getBlockByNumber (L2) numbers with on-chain instants; Dave documents that its node does not start there, and I did not check whether crisium refuses such chains.
Not covered: MachineValidityProof / OutputValidityProof encoding in prt-ethereum.lua (A5), and the per-observation rescan cost already reported as R1-R12-3 / R1-A8-1 / R1-BOUNDARY-1/3.
No experiment on the local chain harness (anvil + Dave) or the player restart runner was run; evidence is code reading plus one heap measurement with a fake chain.
